title: Profile Taxonomy & Release Playbook for GPU SKU Benchmarks
creator: Aria Chen
description:
Objective:
Create a repeatable taxonomy and operational playbook for producing, signing, validating, and publishing hardware-specific performance profiles for our supported GPU SKUs (A100, H100, L40S, MI300). Profiles produced by this playbook must be machine-readable artifacts that drive automated pinning, rollout decisions, and observability in Console and Dedicated control planes.

Background and motivation:
We frequently onboard model variants and hardware SKUs with ad-hoc artifacts. This causes confusion for customers pinning to a model + profile, inconsistent rollouts, and difficulty auditing performance regressions. A clear taxonomy and signing/publishing flow will:
- standardize expectations for latency/throughput/stability per sequence length bin,
- enable safe canary rollouts that target only compatible hardware variants,
- provide traceable signed artifacts for audits and upgrades.

Proposed taxonomy (three-tier):
1) canonical_profile: the minimal public profile describing model architecture, nominal tokenization, and reference sequence bins. Lightweight and stable.
2) calibrated_profile: SKU-specific calibrated numbers (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput at target batch sizes, memory headroom) produced by the calibration harness for a particular GPU SKU and driver/stack. Includes kernel version and quantization flags.
3) experimental_profile: short-lived, best-effort profiles produced during change windows (new kernels/quant stacks) for internal validation only. Marked NOT_FOR_PRODUCTION.

Profile content (artifact fields):
- profile_id (semver-like): e.g. 2025.1.ENG-25401
- model_hash (sha256) and model_version
- sku (A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB, MI300-64GB)
- sequences_binned: [short, medium, long] with representative prompts
- metrics: latency P50/P95/P99, throughput @ batch sizes, memory_peak, kernel_fallback_counts
- accuracy_deltas: top-level eval delta vs baseline on standard prompt set (float)
- ci_signature: signature reference (S3 key + detached sig)
- publisher, created_at, runtime_stack (cuda/rocm versions), notes

Signing and artifact registry:
- Profiles must be signed with a CI key. The artifact payload is uploaded to an immutable S3 path (profiles/YYYY/MM/DD/profile_id.json) and a detached signature file profile_id.json.sig is stored alongside.
- CI publishes a registry index entry (profiles-index.json) that includes profile_id, sku, model_hash, publisher, signature_sha256, and a status (draft/canary/released/revoked).
- Long-term: replace CI key with HSM-backed signing; current next step is to store private key in Vault and rotate quarterly.

Validation and benchmark requirements (CI stage):
- Run synthetic benchmark for each sequence bin: 1000 requests per bin across 3 load shapes (single-stream latency, small-batch concurrency, high-throughput batching).
- Stability: no OOMs and <0.5% kernel-fallback rate (configurable per SKU).
- Latency baselines: for each SKU+model+bin set an upper bound that must not be exceeded by >10% vs reference calibrated_profile.
- Accuracy regression: <0.5% top-1 delta on eval harness for generative/structured output models; <1% for quantized variants.
- Cost signal: normalized tokens-per-second * GPU-hour must be computed and reported.

Canary & rollout policy (published in Console):
- Canary stages: internal-only -> 1% traffic -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%. Each stage requires a 24h hold with observability checks.
- Targeting: canaries are routed to workers pinned to the SKU that the profile was calibrated for. We allow cross-SKU fallbacks only if explicit compatibility is declared in the profile.
- Rollback triggers: +error-rate > 0.5% absolute, latency P95 increased > 20% relative to previous released profile, throughput decreased > 15%, or resource anomalies (OOMs) observed. Automatic rollback should be enabled for P0 releases.

Publishing pipeline (high-level):
1) PR with profile generation config -> bench CI job runs calibration harness across declared SKUs
2) Validation job (accuracy + stability) -> if pass, CI uploads artifact to staging S3 and posts a draft registry entry
3) Release engineer reviews logs + dashboards -> mark registry entry CANARY and promote to canary channel in Console
4) After successful canary window, promote to RELEASED and update Console catalog and release notes

Observability and dashboards:
- Per-profile dashboard: P50/P95/P99 latency over time, throughput, error rate, GPU utilization, memory pressure, kernel fallback counts, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Diff view: show delta between two profile IDs for the same model+sku across bins and highlight regressions beyond thresholds.
- Alerting: automated SLO checks for latency and error rate tied to the rollback triggers above.

Pinning semantics and customer migration:
- Customer-facing pin format: model:version@profile_id (e.g., rw-model-7b:v2@2025.1.ENG-25401)
- When a new profile is RELEASED for the same model+sku we create a migration suggestion with risk_score computed from bench delta, hardware availability delta, and past rollout incidents.
- Customers on Dedicated who explicitly pin to a profile will not be auto-migrated. We will provide a one-click migration flow in Console with a preflight run that simulates 1% traffic and reports expected delta.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- README and playbook written with step-by-step commands to generate a calibrated_profile for all four SKUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300).
- CI bench jobs implemented and green for the short sequence bin for at least one model.
- Profile artifact schema documented and example artifacts uploaded to staging S3.
- Registry index implemented with draft -> canary -> released states and signature verification in release flow.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: signature key compromise. Mitigation: rotate keys, HSM roadmap, and ability to revoke profiles in the registry.
- Risk: customers on older pinned profiles experience regression when we auto-recommend migrations. Mitigation: conservative risk scoring and explicit opt-in for auto-migration.
- Risk: benchmark noise across shared infra. Mitigation: prefer dedicated CI hosts for calibration runs and require multiple runs to compute median metrics.

Open questions for engineering/PM/security:
- Should profile signatures be verifiable by customers (public key distribution) or remain internal?
- How to represent multi-SKU compatibility matrix when models behave differently across SKUs (e.g., memory vs kernel maturity)?
- Where to store long-term audit log of profile promotions (S3 + Dynamo/metadata store?)

Next steps and owners:
- (Eng) Implement bench CI scaffolding and run 1st pass for short bin on A100/H100 (owner: Marcus V.).
- (Infra) Provision dedicated calibration runner instances for stable runs (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- (PM) Draft console UX for profile catalog and migration suggestion (owner: Lina Morales).
- (Security) Review signing flow and key storage (owner: Owen Park).

Artifacts and links (PRs/Logs will be linked in comments):
- Example staging artifact: s3://redwood-profiles/staging/2025.1.ENG-25401.json
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/bench/PR-xxxx

If accepted, this playbook will be used as the canonical process for subsequent model onboardings and for the runtime-1.19 release profile publishing cadence.
